name: Visual-diagnosis roll-call ('This is X. This is X. That's X.' symptom montage → hidden cause)

shots.visual: Close-up: a green mark on a finger
A flaking chain on a neck
Hard stop on a black frame
shots.audio_text: "It's not your skin. It's the metal."

shots.visual: The fix: PVD stack in the shower, then in the sea
shots.audio_text: "14K PVD over stainless steel. Nothing to wear off."

prompts.prompt: Cut every 1.5-2s, identical caption style and position on each "this is" clip, a beat of silence before the turn, then music in.
Use real photos of real wear (team or customers with permission); no makeup-faked damage.

references.author: thousif_maker
references.note: A fitness-app ad that opens like a body diagnosis: a trainer stands behind a woman and points at her stomach, caption "All plus-size girls need to do this to get rid of belly fat". It then cuts to an app screen ('Lazy easy workout') with a short routine list while a woman does the moves on a bed. The format points at a visible sign, names its cause, then shows the fix.

qa_checklist: Hook lands in the first 1.5 s (video) or is readable at thumbnail size (static / slide 1).
Removal test: delete the product from the script. If it still makes sense, rewrite so the product is the payoff.
Matches the reference structure (same beat order and length band) before any creative twist.
Uses only real product imagery for the product; AI is for backgrounds, characters or b-roll, and is disclosed where required.
Every claim is on the brand's approved-claims list (PDP); no invented stats, reviews, doctors or customers.
Captions burned in and inside the safe zone; sound-off still understandable.
One clear CTA that matches the landing page offer.
Three hook variants delivered for the same body (test hooks, not whole new ads).
Avoid: No medical diagnosis framing ("this is an allergy").
Avoid: Use only real examples of wear.
Avoid: Keep the montage short; three examples is enough.
